title: An Interview: The Decision That Changed Everything

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: You took a scholarship to study in Prague at 18, when most people would have stayed close to home. Looking back, how different would your life have been if you hadn't gone?

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Completely different. If I hadn't gone to Prague, I wouldn't have studied international law. I probably would have studied in Aktobe or Almaty — which is fine, but my perspective would have been narrower.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Were there moments when you nearly didn't go?

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Yes. My father was ill that year. If his condition hadn't stabilised in July, I would have deferred the place. I had the form ready to send.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: And if you had deferred — what would have happened?

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: The scholarship would have been withdrawn. It was non-deferrable. So if I'd deferred, I wouldn't have gone to Prague at all. A different life entirely.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: You've described the Czech language as the key that opened your research. What do you mean?

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: If I speak Czech, I can access legal archives that are not translated. If you want to work on Central European constitutional law, you need the primary sources. Without Czech, my research would be derivative — based entirely on what others had already translated and interpreted.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: What would you say to a Kazakhstani student who is considering studying abroad but is afraid?

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: I'd say: if you don't go, you'll always wonder. The discomfort passes. The experience doesn't. And if I hadn't had that discomfort — two years of real struggle in a foreign country — I wouldn't be the researcher I am now. The struggle was the education.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: One final question. If you could go back and give advice to yourself at 18, what would you say?

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: I'd tell myself: trust the discomfort. If things were easy from the start, they wouldn't be worth doing. And I'd warn him not to call home every day for the first month — it makes it harder.

questions.text: Which sentence from the dialogue uses zero conditional?
opts: "If I hadn't gone, I wouldn't have studied law."
"If I speak Czech, I can access legal archives."
"If things were easy, they wouldn't be worth doing."
"If you don't go, you'll always wonder."
questions.correct: "If I speak Czech, I can access legal archives."
questions.hint: Present + present = zero conditional. "If I speak Czech, I CAN access..." — factual relationship. ✅

questions.text: "If I hadn't gone to Prague, I wouldn't have studied international law." — Third conditional because:
opts: He DID go to Prague — this imagines the alternative past that didn't happen
questions.correct: He DID go to Prague — this imagines the alternative past that didn't happen
questions.hint: Third conditional = he actually went to Prague, but imagines the alternative (not going). Counterfactual past. ✅

questions.text: "If things WERE easy from the start, they WOULDN'T be worth doing." — Second conditional because:
opts: Things are not easy, and the speaker imagines a hypothetical where they were — about current reality
questions.correct: Things are not easy, and the speaker imagines a hypothetical where they were — about current reality
questions.hint: Second conditional = things are NOT easy (reality), but imagines "if they were" (hypothetical present). ✅

questions.text: "If you don't go, you'll always wonder." — This is:
opts: First conditional — real future consequence of not going
questions.correct: First conditional — real future consequence of not going
questions.hint: if + present simple + will = first conditional. Real, possible future consequence. ✅

questions.text: "If I ___ that discomfort, I ___ the researcher I am now." (3rd→mixed)
questions.hint: Past condition (3rd type: hadn't had) + present result (2nd type: wouldn't BE now) = mixed conditional. ✅
